title: Rice
lede: Rice contamination depends on chemical species, grain fraction, growing conditions and preparation. The evidence explains why lower arsenic does not always mean lower cadmium, why processing effects differ, and what measurements can support sourcing and food decisions.

scope.geography_market: Source-specific international grain and food surveys, experimental growing settings and human cohorts; no population-weighted worldwide estimate
scope.period: Historical source-specific sampling periods; selected original-publication checks through 2026-10-18
scope.comparator_outcome: Occurrence, source-specific interventions and decision requirements; not certification
scope.analytes: Arsenic species, cadmium, lead, mercury species, nickel, chromium and bounded uranium observations; source-specific coverage, not all-analyte completion
scope.material_form: Rice grain: white/polished and brown/wholegrain; cooked forms identified; derivatives separate
scope.basis: Source-specific grain, dry, as-sold, cooked-food and liquid bases retained; no universal conversion
scope.stage: Cultivation, milling, cooking, ingredient procurement and finished food

answers.text: Rice can contain [[metals/arsenic-inorganic|inorganic arsenic]] and cadmium, with concentrations that vary by growing conditions, grain form and preparation. This review also covers lead, nickel, chromium and mercury where rice-specific evidence is available. Historical surveys describe the rice sampled at that time, so they cannot provide a universal rice concentration or rank current suppliers.

Choosing a control means looking at arsenic and cadmium together. Water management can lower arsenic while increasing cadmium in some soils, though this does not happen everywhere. Both need to be monitored under the relevant growing conditions. Milling and cooking can also change contaminants and nutrients in different ways. Buyers can use the [supplier brief](#from-historical-surveys-to-current-lots) and [dated requirement comparisons](#rice-requirements) to identify what to check for the delivered material and its intended use. Household guidance addresses suitable preparation and dietary variety, with separate precautions for infant feeding.

This is still a partial assessment. Some comparisons remain uncertain because source details are unresolved, studies share samples, or measurements of what remains after treatment are incomplete. Historical surveys and experiments cannot establish current lot performance. Food concentrations and exposure biomarkers alone also cannot establish an individual health effect.

diagram.title: Where rice controls act

stages.label: Before harvest
stages.text: Water, soil and cultivar choices affect what reaches the grain.

stages.label: During manufacture
stages.text: Source qualification, processing, formulation and lot testing address the delivered food.

stages.label: At home
stages.text: Suitable preparation and dietary variety address how rice is consumed.

diagram.caption_omission_reason: Redundant with the preceding sourcing and production paragraph; trade-offs remain beside the relevant claims.

answers.text: This page covers edible rice grain, including brown, white and cooked rice. Brown rice retains the bran and germ; polishing removes outer tissues to produce white rice. Grain fractions, prepared foods and rice-derived ingredients need separate interpretation because processing can change both composition and measurement basis.

Flour, bran, syrup, protein powder and beverages are distinct materials. Their results can inform a grain assessment, but they cannot be assigned to untested rice products using a common conversion factor.

Use the material, chemical species and preparation reported in each study. The table below defines the main boundaries; the later sections explain occurrence, processing and controls in detail. Uncooked rice is a food form; a moisture-free dry-weight result is an analytical basis. The two descriptions are not interchangeable.

cells: Brown and white grain
Keep grain fraction and cultivar explicit. Matched brown/white measurements show that metals do not all respond alike to polishing.
Cooked rice
Prepared-food composites describe the sampled food after preparation. Compare concentrations only on a compatible moisture and preparation basis.
Derived ingredients and foods
Syrup, protein, flour, drinks and specialized formulas require their own composition and preparation evidence. Grain results do not establish the final product concentration.

passages.text: For this parent page, derivative studies explain where grain evidence stops transferring. A drink, specialized formula or protein powder must retain its own formulation, processing and preparation instructions. Rice drinks and medically formulated infant feeds are distinct products; their measurements should not be substituted for one another.
passages.question: Can rice drinks and rice-based infant formulas be treated as the same material?

answers.text: Rice occurrence studies cover different chemical species, grain forms and sampling frames. The table brings international surveys, field-grown grain, commercial rice products and FDA cooked-rice composites together by analyte, while retaining each source’s reported statistic and measurement basis. A mean, median and detected range answer different questions; the table labels each explicitly.
answers.heading: Arsenic species and occurrence evidence

passages.text: Arsenic is a group of chemically distinct measurements. [[metals/arsenic-total|Total arsenic]] includes inorganic arsenic and organic species; inorganic arsenic usually combines arsenite and arsenate. Dimethylarsinic acid (DMA) is often present in rice and can vary independently. A total-arsenic result therefore cannot be converted into measured inorganic arsenic using a universal percentage. The same separation is needed between total mercury and methylmercury, and between total chromium and Cr(VI).
passages.question: Can total arsenic stand in for inorganic arsenic?

passages.text: EFSA’s 2024 organoarsenic assessment adds a separate evidence stream. Its occurrence analysis includes DMA measurements in polished and brown grain, while some processed-food estimates are derived using recipes and an assumption of no processing loss. Direct grain observations and model-derived flour, porridge or beverage values must remain distinguishable. Organic arsenic is not one interchangeable substance with one toxicological interpretation.

answers.text: Sampling and censoring matter as much as the reported concentration. The global cadmium compilation reuses earlier studies and substitutes half the detection limit for low results. The Henan monitoring summaries also include substituted non-detects. Their reported medians remain usable source summaries, but they are not medians of detected samples and cannot supply a matched trend against the FDA composites.
answers.heading: Sampling, censoring and shared observations

passages.text: Source rows preserve the counted unit. The Vietnamese field study covers genotypes with paired brown and white grain; the Ethiopian study combines farmers’ grain into area composites. Multiple analyte rows reuse those same materials. Neither more rows nor technical repeats create additional independent studies.

answers.text: Direct mercury measurements remain separate from model outputs. Brombach’s European survey reports both total mercury and methylmercury in a mixture of grain and rice products; its overall range cannot be assigned to a grain-only or baby-food subgroup. Cui’s spatial model addresses a different question and does not contribute a new measured product distribution to this table.
answers.heading: Mercury species and comparison boundaries

passages.text: Original source means, medians, ranges and measurement bases remain visible. Recovered individual measurements and regional summaries supply compatible HMI references; the baseline does not require every study to report a percentile. Unknown moisture bases and unresolved reporting limits remain explicit. Neither below-LOQ results nor an absence of detections establishes zero contamination.

Grain forms, preparation bases, sampling designs, periods and censoring conventions affect interpretation. The HMI baseline pools compatible historical evidence across studies using equal family weights and a common subgroup-median layer. Its original statistics, basis conversions and sensitivity checks appear in the sidebar. A finding can remain unclassified when its reporting bounds span categories or no compatible reference is available.
passages.question: Why is there no single worldwide rice concentration?

passages.text: A kilogram of dried grain and a kilogram of cooked rice containing absorbed water are different measurement bases. Converting mg/kg to µg/kg changes the unit only; it does not correct for water uptake, milling yield or preparation. Such comparisons need the source-specific moisture or yield information.
passages.question: Can dry-grain and cooked-rice concentrations be compared directly?

presentation.text: Low, Moderate and High show position against a scoped HMI baseline. Open a result for its reference, methods and limitations.

context_intro.text: HMI pools compatible evidence across sampling families to calculate fixed rice references. The dry-grain references combine FDA category medians with Carey regional medians for inorganic arsenic and DMA, FDA with Myanmar township medians for total arsenic, and Myanmar with Shi country medians for cadmium. Native-moisture references combine Saudi and Myanmar grain evidence using the Myanmar study’s measured 6–7% moisture loss. Each family receives equal weight; its subgroups share that weight. These references describe subgroup medians in the evidence library, not the median of all rice sold worldwide. Each row’s reported mean or median is compared with that reference; means are never relabelled as medians. Cooked rice remains separate. Low is below Q1, Moderate is Q1–Q3, and High is above Q3; reporting bounds must support one position. The sidebar shows contributing families, conversions, count-weighted and leave-one-family-out sensitivity, and the limitations of single-family references. These are concentration positions, not safety or certainty grades.

answers.text: Flooding changes the soil chemistry that controls plant exposure. Reducing conditions can dissolve iron phases that retain arsenic and favor more mobile arsenic species in porewater. Drying changes these reactions and can increase cadmium availability. Limmer’s experiment links water regimes to grain As and Cd; Seyfferth’s broader outcome analysis also measures mercury species and methane. These results connect a manipulated growing condition with an edible-grain endpoint.
answers.heading: Soil water, redox and grain uptake

passages.text: The pathway is not simply “more soil metal means proportionally more grain metal.” Mineral binding, pH, redox, microbial transformations and plant transport affect availability. A soil screening result identifies an environmental question; a grain measurement answers the food-composition question. Market observations alone cannot identify whether a particular lot’s metal came from geology, irrigation, fertilizer or atmospheric deposition.
passages.question: Does a high soil concentration predict the grain concentration?

passages.text: The response varies across growing conditions. In the Arkansas production-field study, multiple aerations were associated with a 31% lower median grain inorganic arsenic than conventional flooding, while cadmium did not show a statistically significant water-management effect. This observational comparison is a regional counterexample to an inevitable cadmium increase. It does not establish equivalence or a universal reduction factor. The paper’s field-year denominator differs between Methods and Table 1; its summary concentrations remain outside the comparison tables pending reconciliation.

answers.text: Microorganisms can change arsenic species before plant uptake. Dai and colleagues combine field observations, soil chronosequences, incubations and a global metagenomic survey to examine the balance between arsenic methylation and demethylation. This links microbial functions with grain speciation and straighthead disease. It does not mean that a larger methylated fraction is automatically nutritionally preferable or that a proposed microbial manipulation has established commercial benefit.
answers.heading: Microbial and plant mechanisms

passages.text: Cheng and colleagues compare two rice cultivars and their root-associated microbiomes under soil amendments. The lower-accumulating cultivar also had distinctive microbial and soil features. Such coupled findings make biological mechanisms plausible, but a microbial association or predictive model is not by itself proof that adding one organism will lower harvested-grain cadmium under another field’s conditions.

Mishra’s arsenic work examines species transformation and thiol binding in exposed rice plants. Inoue’s Nramp5 engineering study uses a yeast assay to examine cadmium and manganese uptake selectivity. These studies help explain transport and retention; their experimental systems do not provide a market-rice concentration distribution or a demonstrated reduction in dietary exposure.

answers.text: Contamination attribution requires measurements along the proposed route. Paired irrigation-water, soil, plant and grain samples can test a pathway; source tracing must also consider alternative inputs and collection timing. A high concentration in a retail package does not reveal the responsible field process. Likewise, cleaning up an analytical extract removes interference for measurement; it is not evidence that the food itself has been decontaminated.

Origin can inform investigation, but its meaning depends on the survey. Carey’s and Shi’s international studies target market rice with unequal geographic coverage, whereas the FDA regions are collection markets. A US collection-region label does not identify growing origin. Country and region differences can also reflect cultivar, milling, water management, harvest period and detection-limit treatment, so they cannot be read as fixed properties of all future shipments.
answers.heading: Geography and sampling frame

answers.text: Cultivar studies demonstrate that genetics matters within a defined environment. Liu’s ionomic association study examines rice accessions under contrasting growing conditions, and Tran’s Vietnamese landrace study measures both brown and white grain. Genetic associations identify candidate loci and breeding hypotheses; stable low accumulation requires confirmation across soils, water regimes and seasons while retaining acceptable yield and essential-element uptake. The number of accessions is not a number of independent studies.
answers.heading: Cultivar, environment and changing conditions

passages.text: Muehe’s greenhouse experiment examines climate and soil arsenic together and finds that their combined effects can alter rice yield and grain arsenic. It is a treatment-specific experiment, not a prediction that every future crop will show the same percentage change. It strengthens the case for testing cultivar performance under the growing conditions in which it will actually be used.
passages.question: What does the climate experiment tell us about future crops?

answers.text: The FDA comparison calculates a matched historical change rather than a national trend. Across five shared winter-region groups, cooked white-rice cadmium medians change from 4.3 to 5.0 µg/kg and brown-rice medians from 5.5 to 9.8 µg/kg between FY2018 and FY2020. The matching uses six earlier and five later composites. The drawer retains the unmatched source summaries, so readers can distinguish the comparison subset from the full dataset.

passages.text: Within-lot and between-lot variability remain separate purchasing questions. Composite surveys smooth some individual-item variability, and repeated analytical runs improve measurement precision without creating new independent lots. A supplier claim needs current, identifiable lots and a sampling design suited to the shipment or process decision; a historical country median cannot replace that evidence.

answers.text: Brown and white rice do not have one universal contaminant ranking. Polishing redistributes material between edible white grain and removed fractions. Tran’s matched brown/white analysis shows that many elements decline with polishing, while cadmium does not follow the same pattern. This prevents a blanket “polishing removes heavy metals” conclusion. Bran and other by-products also need characterization if they enter human food, supplements or feed; the metal removed from one fraction has not necessarily left the wider food chain.
answers.heading: How do brown and white rice compare?

passages.text: The Vietnamese landrace experiment measured brown and white grain from the same plants. Most measured elements were higher in brown grain, but cadmium and molybdenum were exceptions. This is stronger evidence about the effect of grain fraction than a retail comparison of unrelated brown and white products. It also shows why an arsenic benefit from polishing cannot automatically be assigned to cadmium.
passages.question: What does the matched brown-versus-white comparison add?

answers.text: Rinsing alone has limited arsenic benefit; FDA guidance also notes possible nutrient losses from rinsing or excess-water cooking of enriched rice. Cooking methods need their own evidence. Carey’s cooking experiments distinguish excess-water cooking from percolation. At a 12:1 water:rice ratio, the study reports 57 ± 5% lower residual-grain inorganic arsenic across the tested materials; the meaning of the reported uncertainty term remains unresolved here. That result concerns the tested method and endpoint, not a common reduction factor for cadmium, methylmercury or all household cooking.
answers.heading: Does rinsing or cooking reduce arsenic?

passages.text: Pogoson’s process is substantially different: sequential chemical soaks, each lasting 12 hours, followed by cooking. The primary manuscript reports reductions in Cd, inorganic As and DMA, but the starting-species quantities in the stored extraction need arm and basis reconciliation. The process belongs in the evidence on potential preprocessing; it should not be presented as ordinary rinsing or a validated household instruction.
passages.question: Are chemical soaking studies equivalent to ordinary rinsing?

passages.text: Removal into discarded water differs from dilution by water retained in cooked food. A process comparison should retain the starting and residual food concentration, food yield, water quality, drainage and waste destination. FDA guidance also notes that some excess-water methods reduce nutrients. Reusing contaminated water or ignoring the discarded stream can change the exposure or environmental consequence.

answers.text: Derivative evidence confirms the need to measure the final material. Hosojima’s protein-powder study includes a contaminant composition table, while Zhao tests microbial immobilization to remove cadmium from contaminated rice flour. One describes a specific ingredient used in a nutrition trial; the other evaluates a processing method. Neither supplies a universal grain-to-protein or grain-to-flour conversion, and laboratory removal requires separate process-safety and residual-food validation.
answers.heading: Syrup, protein, flour and drinks

passages.text: Jackson’s rice-syrup-containing foods and D’Amato’s Italian-market beverages show why formulation and material identity travel with the result. The beverage study separately measures arsenic species, rather than estimating inorganic arsenic from a generic total-arsenic fraction. Its liquid-food concentrations cannot be compared directly with dry grain without accounting for rice inclusion and water. The [[regulations/eu2023-arsenic-rice-based-drinks|rice-based-drink regulatory scope]] is a distinct category with a selected EU provision shown in the requirements table.

EFSA’s organoarsenic assessment describes thiolated species and evidence of transformation during processing, storage and acidic extraction. Its processed-commodity scenarios partly assume no DMA loss. These models cannot establish what actually happens in a particular puffed, stored or hydrolysed product. Species-preserving measurements and the relevant original processing studies are needed to resolve that question.

A useful process calculation measures metal mass in the incoming rice and in each outgoing food, bran, water or sorbent stream, alongside moisture and yield. A lower concentration in a wetter product can occur without the same reduction in total metal mass. A process that transfers metal to waste also requires a disposal assessment; testing only the final concentration leaves that question unanswered.
passages.question: What would demonstrate actual metal removal rather than dilution?

answers.text: The table below groups rice controls by where they can be applied: agronomic measures during cultivation, manufacturing controls during sourcing and processing, and consumer choices during preparation and consumption. It brings together measured interventions, market comparisons and agency guidance, with their different scopes and limitations.
Compare effects alongside the study conditions, residual contamination and practical trade-offs. A percentage reduction alone does not establish which option is most effective.

Each row keeps the measured contaminants together, including adverse effects; filtering for one analyte retains the linked outcomes so that an arsenic reduction can be read alongside a cadmium increase.

passages.text: Compare the same chemical species, food material, starting condition and endpoint. Then check the absolute residual concentration, uncertainty, other contaminant changes, nutrients and operating conditions. A large relative decrease can leave an important residual concentration; a historical market contrast or agency recommendation is not an experimental treatment effect.
passages.question: How should two controls with different percentage reductions be compared?

answers.text: The best contaminant result depends on what else is measured. Drier irrigation can lower arsenic and mercury species and methane while increasing cadmium; the same management change may also affect yield and micronutrients. A cadmium increase is conditional: the Arkansas production-field comparison found no significant water-management effect on grain cadmium. Paired grain monitoring is therefore more informative than assuming that every drying regime shifts contamination toward cadmium. These linked outcomes explain why optimizing only arsenic can give a misleading assessment of the crop. A treatment with a large percentage reduction can still leave an important residual concentration.
answers.heading: Contaminants, nutrients and yield

passages.text: A yield benefit is not evidence of a contaminant benefit. Gupta’s ash trials are a useful counterexample: increased yield accompanied no statistically detected change in the measured grain arsenic species or cadmium. Conversely, a contaminant reduction with a yield penalty may be difficult to sustain. Both findings belong in the assessment rather than selecting only favorable endpoints.

answers.text: Polishing and water-intensive cooking can change both contaminants and nutrient composition. The brown/white comparison cannot determine an overall nutritional preference from one arsenic value, and cooking that leaches arsenic can also leach minerals or added nutrients. Net benefit requires the actual diet, food substitution and retained nutrient composition, not an unweighted sum of metal concentrations.

passages.text: Selenium applications illustrate another distinction: an agronomic Cd response, grain selenium enrichment and a clinical benefit are separate outcomes. The field experiment supports investigation of the tested control, while its transfer to commercial enriched rice needs direct grain measurements and nutritional assessment. More of an essential element does not establish less of another contaminant.

answers.text: Water demand, energy, sensory quality, amendment quality and waste handling can determine whether a laboratory process is usable. Chemical soaking creates different operating and disposal requirements from household cooking. Microbial or sorbent removal must also show that food quality and safety remain acceptable. Comparative commercial cost-effectiveness and complete mass balances are not established across the selected controls, so a universal preferred process cannot be assigned.

Sampling should match the decision. An increment, a composite, an analytical replicate and an independent lot are different units. The FDA composites describe prepared-food sampling; Shi’s compilation describes market grain; field treatment plots address agronomic response. None directly supplies a validated acceptance plan for a current shipment. The relevant unresolved quantities include within-lot heterogeneity, between-lot variation and uncertainty around the decision boundary.
answers.heading: Representative material before analytical precision

answers.text: Speciation needs demonstrated recovery and stability in the actual matrix. Navaretnam’s white/brown-rice method and Tian’s inorganic-arsenic assay show distinct analytical approaches. A sensitive instrument or a high calibration correlation does not alone establish extraction completeness, species preservation or agreement at the concentration where a purchasing decision will be made. Matrix validation, blanks, reference materials, recovery and reporting limits remain essential. The [[testing/icp-ms|ICP-MS methods overview]] explains the distinction between elemental measurement and chromatographic speciation.
answers.heading: Species preservation and screening fitness

passages.text: Song’s Cr(VI) method found no detectable Cr(VI) in the small set of tested foods, including rice flour, and showed that recovery depended on whether the spike was introduced before or after extraction and on holding time. This illustrates a species-stability problem: nondetection must be bounded by the tested matrix, method and handling. It cannot prove that all rice is free of Cr(VI).

EFSA similarly notes that acidic extraction can convert thiolated arsenic species into DMA. A chromatographic result may therefore depend on sample handling as well as the original food composition. For transformation studies, recovering total arsenic does not by itself establish that each original species was preserved.
passages.question: Can sample preparation change the reported arsenic species?

answers.text: Portable screening can help target confirmatory analysis, but its decision errors matter. Tian’s magnetic-purification electrochemical grain assay addresses matrix interference before measuring Cd and Pb; the purification occurs in the analytical workflow. Rice-specific bias, uncertainty, false acceptance and false rejection near the relevant boundary are needed before a screening result can substitute for a reference method in a lot decision.

passages.text: A non-detect means the result is below a stated analytical limit under that method. It is not a measured zero, and an unspecified limit cannot establish a useful upper bound. A nonsignificant treatment comparison answers a different question again: it may reflect little effect or imprecision. Neither statement means that a literature search found no relevant evidence.
passages.question: How should a non-detect differ from “no effect” in a report?

table.title: Checks for an interpretable rice test report
headers: What the report needs to establish

cells: Material and sampling
Identify the lot or survey, grain form and preparation. Describe increments, compositing, sample reduction and retained samples; analytical repeats do not measure unobserved lot variability.
Analyte and basis
Name the measured chemical species, units and moisture or preparation basis. Total-element results cannot silently replace a species-specific result.
Method performance
Document matrix validation, extraction recovery, species stability, blanks, reference materials and reporting limits. Calibration correlation alone is insufficient.
Decision uncertainty
Distinguish sampling from analytical uncertainty. A screening method needs evidence about bias and false acceptance or rejection near the intended decision boundary.

answers.text: Use historical origin evidence to decide where to investigate, then qualify the actual material. The arsenic and cadmium surveys show variation within and between growing regions, with sampling limitations and reused observations. A current supplier dossier should identify cultivar, growing origin, harvest, grain form, milling, water management where known and delivered-lot identity. A country label alone cannot demonstrate the joint iAs/Cd/Hg composition of a shipment.
answers.heading: What should a buyer request from a supplier?

answers.text: Specifications should name the intended food use, chemical species, material basis and analytical decision rule. Incoming-rice results need a documented relationship to the final recipe and preparation. Rejection or acceptance near a limit should address measurement uncertainty and sampling fitness; a generic certificate of analysis or a total-arsenic value cannot silently replace a species-specific requirement.

passages.text: The brief below is a practical evidence-request sequence. [Download a reusable copy](../static/data/rice-supplier-testing-brief.txt) and record the material, intended use and market before choosing a numerical comparator.

Where a supplier changes cultivar, farm, water regime, amendment, milling or processing, the previous qualification may no longer describe the delivered material. The field evidence makes these changes plausible effect modifiers. Verify them with relevant grain and finished-food results rather than assuming a historical reduction percentage will persist.
passages.question: When should a supplier or process be requalified?

cells: 1 · Identify the purchase
Record rice form, intended product, destination market, consumer age group, supplier and lot, harvest and growing origin.
2 · Select the applicable requirements
Match analyte, category and marketed-food basis to the primary instrument. Include nickel for EU rice and inorganic arsenic for the relevant rice use; retain the instrument version and date.
3 · Request the laboratory evidence

Obtain the sampling plan and lot link, measured species, units, moisture/preparation basis, methods, reporting limits, recoveries and uncertainty. Resolve a missing inorganic-arsenic result rather than treating total arsenic as the same measurement.
4 · Interpret the result
Compare compatible bases and document the decision rule and unresolved sampling or analytical uncertainty. A historical occurrence range supplies context, not a shipment acceptance result.
5 · Verify changes and the finished food
Reassess cultivar, origin, irrigation, milling and formulation changes with suitable grain and finished-product results. Record what remains unknown and who resolves the release decision.

answers.text: Commercial evidence should be assessed rather than assumed absent. Li’s regional programme demonstrates a longer implementation horizon, while Sun and Jiang provide multiyear field observations. The remaining purchasing questions are narrower: which farms and lots were actually sampled, what residual concentrations and uncertainty were observed, how the practices persisted, and what they cost under the buyer’s conditions. Programme reach is not the same as the number of independent sampled farms.

Grain findings do not transfer directly to rice drinks or [[products/baby-cereals-dry-rice-based|dry rice-based infant cereal]]. Finished foods need direct evidence or a verified formulation model. Jackson’s rice-syrup-containing products, Meyer’s hydrolysed-rice formulas and D’Amato’s beverages differ in composition and use. Gu’s Australian infant-food survey also separates rice-based categories and measured analytes. A grain concentration cannot be assigned wholesale to cereal, crackers, protein powder, syrup or a drink, and an analyte not measured in one category cannot be inferred from another category’s result.
answers.heading: Which findings apply to rice drinks or infant cereal?

passages.text: EFSA’s rice-formula DMA scenario reuses Meyer’s measurements with explicit reconstitution and consumption assumptions. It is not an additional independent formula survey, and its assumed dilution is not a universal preparation factor. Ingredient inclusion, moisture, processing yield, other ingredients and preparation water all need to be identified before estimating consumed dose.

answers.text: Bioaccessibility, absorption and chemical extraction are different endpoints. An in-vitro digestion experiment measures what becomes soluble under its specified gastrointestinal model; human absorption requires biological evidence. Cardini’s methods study identifies cadmium-binding compounds using chemical extraction and chromatographic techniques. A low extraction yield in that workflow cannot be used as a low human-absorption percentage or as proof that the original food poses little exposure.
answers.heading: Biomarkers, exposure and health outcomes

passages.text: The infant studies require careful study identity. The 2017 Belfast report includes 79 pre-weaning infants and an 11-infant paired subset. The separate 2018 New Hampshire study follows 15 paired infants and reports higher urinary arsenic species during weaning, with associations involving rice cereal, fruit and vegetables. These data support exposure investigation, but diet and age change together; the biomarker is not a rice-specific disease endpoint.

Du’s clinic cohort provides a useful null comparison: among 56 infants with reflux or dysphagia, total urinary arsenic did not differ statistically between thickener groups (p=0.086). The small, observational groups do not establish equivalence or justify changing prescribed feeding. A null thickener comparison also does not negate the dietary associations in a different cohort with different exposures and sampling.

Pregnancy adds physiological and metabolic complexity to urinary arsenic interpretation. Ashley-Martin’s review explains why species, timing, metabolism and exposure sources matter. A urine concentration should not be attributed to rice without considering drinking water and other foods, nor should urinary DMA automatically be equated with the amount of inorganic arsenic eaten.

answers.text: Rothenberg’s rural-China cohort links a prenatal exposure biomarker with child development, rather than measuring an intervention on rice. In adjusted models, doubling maternal hair total mercury corresponded to a 1.3-point lower mental-development score (95% CI −2.6 to −0.14); the psychomotor estimate’s interval included no association. Follow-up declined from 391 enrolled mothers to 190 children assessed at 36 months. Hair total mercury was the measured proxy, and attrition, caregiving and confounding limit a rice-specific causal interpretation.

passages.text: Modeled risk and observed disease must also remain separate. Song’s intake assessment multiplies food concentrations by consumption, while Huang’s meta-analysis includes hazard calculations whose combined-metal result must be distinguished from individual-metal quotients. These are exposure or risk models, not measured illness rates or a diagnosis for a reader. No individual risk prediction is generated from the occurrence explorer.

answers.text: Requirements depend on species, rice form, intended use and jurisdiction. The selected EU provisions below were checked against the consolidation dated 19 August 2026 and the nickel amendment; FDA’s final infant-rice-cereal guidance remains nonbinding and enforcement-relevant. This is a dated selection, not a complete list of applicable analytes, jurisdictions or finished-food requirements.
answers.heading: Requirements and toxicological context

passages.text: EU maximum levels generally apply to the edible food as placed on the market, unless the entry specifies otherwise. They are not automatically moisture-free dry-weight limits. Nickel rice entries apply from 1 July 2026; the regulation retains its transition for food lawfully placed on the market earlier. For processed or compound foods without a specific maximum, Article 3 requires justified concentration, dilution, processing and ingredient factors. A cooked-rice literature value cannot be compared directly with an uncooked-grain requirement without a supported basis relationship. Article 4 also prohibits deliberate chemical detoxification of covered food; a laboratory removal result is not authorization to use that process commercially.

Toxicological reference points answer a different question from food-law limits. EFSA’s inorganic-arsenic and organoarsenic assessments evaluate different chemical species and uncertainties. Their modeled exposure and margin-of-exposure scenarios should retain their assumptions and source datasets. A legal maximum, health reference point and descriptive survey percentile cannot be substituted for one another.

answers.text: This is a structured comparative synthesis of selected ingested research, not a completed systematic review. It connects occurrence, mechanisms, interventions, product composition and human exposure while preserving their different study designs. The local evidence map also contains records whose exact findings remain unresolved. No pooled worldwide concentration, overall safety score or outcome-level certainty grade is assigned from publication counts.
answers.heading: What this assessment establishes

passages.text: Several limitations can materially change the interpretation: reused global-survey samples and related experimental reports, uncertain processing bases, incomplete species preservation, and missing absolute residual effects or precision. Historical market samples do not establish current supplier performance. An association in a cohort does not establish that changing rice alone would alter the health outcome. These limits accompany the conclusions rather than being hidden in the source index.

The selected FDA and intervention explorers remain deliberately scoped to their reconciled datasets. The expanded narrative includes additional research whose observations have not all been reconciled into the same comparable row structure. Original tables, independent sample units, uncertainty and overlapping study families must be resolved before adding such findings to a quantitative comparison.

answers.text: The most consequential remaining work concerns source accuracy and identity, compatible occurrence extraction, paired intervention residuals and uncertainty, species transformation during processing and storage, validated lot sampling, and exposure attribution. Several stored summaries contain conflicting arithmetic, species or compliance interpretations. The affected claims are withheld here; an unresolved extraction is not presented as proof that no evidence exists.
answers.heading: Evidence still needed

passages.text: For agricultural controls, the next useful evidence is jointly measured residual Cd, iAs and relevant Hg species, alongside yield, nutrients, independent field units, durability, resource use and cost. For processing, it is a paired mass balance and species-preserving analysis of food and waste streams. For products and health, it is exact formulation and consumption context plus appropriately adjusted, uncertainty-bearing outcome estimates. These are specific limits on present decisions, rather than a demand for more papers regardless of relevance.

The starting inventory is the existing rice-linked source corpus, supplemented by targeted checks of original publications and authorities. Screening and question-specific external searching are incomplete; some original files are unavailable locally. The bibliography identifies the works actually used in the synthesis and explorers. The separate Sources index is a discovery aid and includes records that have not been accepted as supporting evidence.
passages.question: How were sources selected, and what does the source index mean?

passages.text: The evidence assessment was expanded on 18 October 2026 to distinguish global grain surveys from prepared-food composites, add species and derivative evidence, compare agronomic and processing controls including null findings, and connect food measurements with exposure and health research. New original data, corrected study identity, resolved overlap or material changes in requirements should reopen the affected conclusion.

shareText: Rice controls can lower arsenic while raising cadmium. This evidence review connects grain surveys, processing, field trade-offs and human exposure, with their limits explicit.

quick_read.text: Rice metal levels depend on growing conditions, grain form and preparation. Water management can trade lower inorganic arsenic for higher cadmium.

facets.label: Metals of concern
facets.text: [[metals/arsenic-inorganic|Inorganic arsenic]] and [[metals/cadmium|cadmium]] are central concerns. Lead, total mercury and chromium are also measured; chemical species remain separate.

facets.label: Main drivers
facets.text: Soil, cultivar and water management influence uptake. Bran retention, milling and cooking change the rice material being compared.

facets.label: Practical framing
facets.text: Keep grain and cooked-rice results separate. Excess-water cooking with the water discarded can lower inorganic arsenic; assess cadmium too and verify current supplier lots.
